budget_items.topic: Department of health grant and attendance clerk
budget_items.what_was_said: A grant for this and next school year funds a substitute nurse and a part-time attendance clerk with no benefits.
A mid-year position costing half the salary and insurance; still under consideration for the FY23 budget as part of the capital staffing plan.
A three-year contract with no options; new language says the contractor must request payment for undriven, unrescheduled days, and payment applies only if legislation authorizes it.
Contractors sought partial payment for the first pandemic year and the town settled near the low end of what other districts paid.
Positions are funded by ESSER for three years, after which the district must decide whether to keep them in the budget and what to give up.
Three school items ranked among 31 needs; dollar amounts and what can be funded are not yet known.
The paper has asked for payment for space; the superintendent said the district would fund it if charged.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved the general education transportation bid, a three-year contract with new payment language for undriven, unrescheduled days.
The committee approved permission to post a part-time attendance clerk and a primary school guidance counselor.
It waived the first reading of the student activities policy after adding "or staff"; the second reading is set for the next meeting.
It approved a primary school line-item transfer, moving balances from music lines to general and physical education supplies.
It approved the committee organization chart as amended.

why_it_matters: The bus contract ties payment for days when buses cannot run to legislation authorizing it, so a future pandemic-style closure could add a transportation cost that the contract does not settle in advance.

The guidance counselor is a mid-year position still under consideration for the FY23 budget, and the behavioral health positions funded by ESSER for three years will need a decision on budget space after that, both of which bear on next year's school budget and the town's share of it.
